chunks: My father (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, he said: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from his father from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Muhammad ibn Humran from Abu Ubayda al-Hadhdha', who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said:

O Ziyad! Beware of argumentation, for it creates doubt, nullifies deeds, and degrades its doer. Perhaps a man may say something for which he is not forgiven. O Ziyad! There was once a community who left the knowledge they were entrusted with and sought knowledge they were spared from, until their discourse led them to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and they became perplexed; so much so that if a man were called from in front of him, he would reply from behind, or if called from behind, he would reply from in front.

key_terms.الخصومات: Argumentation/disputes - religious debates that lead to doubt and spiritual harm
key_terms.الشك: Doubt - the first destructive consequence of argumentation
key_terms.تحيروا: Became perplexed - the ultimate consequence of speculating about God's essence

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Baqir say about religious argumentation and its dangers?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) warns his companion Ziyad against religious argumentation, explaining its three destructive consequences: creating doubt, nullifying good deeds, and degrading the arguer. He then illustrates with a cautionary historical example of a community that abandoned obligatory knowledge for prohibited theological speculation about God's essence, becoming so mentally confused they could not even respond to calls from the correct direction.

en.bilal-muhammad: My father (ra) narrated to us. He said: `Abdullah b. Ja`far al-Himyari narrated to us from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. `Isa from his father from Muhammad b. Abi `Umayr from Muhammad b. Humran from Abi `Ubayda al-Hatha’. He said: Abu Ja`far (as) said:

O Ziyad! Beware of argumentation, for it creates doubt, nullifies deeds, and degrades its doer. Perhaps a man may say something that he is not forgiven for. O Ziyad! There was once a community who left the required knowledge and sought unrequired knowledge, until they spoke of Allah [and His essence] and became perplexed by it; [so much so] that if a man were to call in front of them, they would reply to the back, and to the front if called from the back.
